summary.text: Michelle Fischbach is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 7th District, first elected in 2020. A longtime Minnesota state senator, she became the first woman to serve as president of the Minnesota Senate and served as Minnesota's lieutenant governor in 2018-2019. In the House she serves on the Ways and Means and Rules committees and chairs the Rules and Organization of the House Subcommittee.

paragraphs.text: Fischbach grew up in Woodbury, Minnesota, and graduated from Woodbury High School.
She earned a bachelor's degree in political science and economics from St. Cloud State University and a law degree from William Mitchell College of Law.
In 1994 she was elected to the Paynesville city council, becoming its first woman member.
She and her husband, Scott, have lived in the Paynesville area.
Fischbach was elected to the Minnesota Senate in a 1996 special election and served until 2018, including as chair of the Senate Higher Education Committee.
In 2011 she became the first woman in Minnesota history to serve as President of the Minnesota Senate, a post she held until 2013 and again from 2017.

In 2018, after Lt. Gov. Tina Smith was appointed to the U.S. Senate, Fischbach became the 49th Lieutenant Governor of Minnesota because the Senate president is next in the line of succession; she served until January 2019.
She won the 2020 election for Minnesota's 7th District, defeating Democratic incumbent Collin Peterson, and took office in January 2021.
Fischbach serves on the Committee on Rules, where she chairs the Rules and Organization of the House Subcommittee, and on the Committee on Ways and Means.
Her official biography lists agriculture, 2nd Amendment rights, respect for law and order, and defending the unborn as the issues that matter most to her district.
She and Scott have two children and seven grandchildren and live on a hobby farm in the Paynesville area.
